subject.title: Feature Request: Pre-tool-call routing hook for model delegation

question: Should OpenClaw expose pre-tool model/session routing as an additive plugin/runtime API, and what authority, context visibility, auth, fallback, and session-state boundaries must that API enforce?
rationale: Source inspection proves the feature gap, but the requested capability crosses plugin trust, provider/model routing, credentials, transcript continuity, approvals, fallback, and audit boundaries that require maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design a typed routing phase
options.body: Add or extend a pre-tool routing contract only after defining allowed context, redirect targets, auth/fallback behavior, audit logs, failure semantics, and compatibility tests.

options.title: Keep hooks params-only
options.body: Leave `before_tool_call` limited to params/block/approval and require users to use prompt-time model selection, explicit subagents, or capability-specific model settings.

options.title: Split context from routing
options.body: First add narrowly gated assistant/tool context visibility, then revisit model/session redirection after a separate security review.

recommendation.title: Design a typed routing phase
recommendation.body: Add or extend a pre-tool routing contract only after defining allowed context, redirect targets, auth/fallback behavior, audit logs, failure semantics, and compatibility tests.

likelyOwner.reason: He already reviewed this exact issue boundary and current blame/history places him near both the hook surface and adjacent model-hook design.
